facts.frequency: When needed for wheeze or breathlessness. Maximum 4 times in 24 hours.
warnings: Your label and leaflet say different things. Ask your pharmacist.
Do not take more than 8 puffs in 24 hours.
Tell your doctor if your usual dose stops working.
Do not use more often than advised.
get_help: Call 999 if you have severe difficulty breathing or swelling of the face or lips.

conflicts.label: TWO puffs
conflicts.leaflet: Usual dose: ONE puff when needed. Adults may take up to 2 puffs if needed.

conflicts.label: When needed for wheeze or breathlessness. Maximum 4 times in 24 hours.
conflicts.leaflet: When needed. Do not take more than 8 puffs in 24 hours.

steps.text_en: Your label and leaflet say different things. Ask your pharmacist.
steps.picture_prompt: a person holding a medicine box and a leaflet, looking unsure

steps.text_en: This is Salbutamol 100 micrograms Evohaler. It is an inhaler for wheeze or breathlessness.
steps.picture_prompt: A blue and grey pressurised inhaler with a cap, standing upright on a table

steps.text_en: Use your inhaler when you wheeze or feel breathless.
steps.picture_prompt: A person sitting on a chair with one hand on their chest, looking short of breath

steps.text_en: Take the cap off your inhaler. Check the mouthpiece is clear.
steps.picture_prompt: Hands holding an inhaler with the cap removed, shaking it gently
Hands holding an inhaler with the cap removed, shaking it gently

steps.text_en: Hold your breath for up to 10 seconds, or as long as is comfortable.
steps.picture_prompt: A person breathing in with an inhaler, then a second picture of the same person holding their breath with cheeks slightly puffed

steps.text_en: Wait at least 30 seconds before your next puff.
steps.picture_prompt: A person rinsing their mouth with water from a glass over a bathroom sink and spitting into the sink
A pharmacist behind a counter holding an inhaler box and a folded leaflet, talking to a customer

steps.text_en: Your leaflet says the usual dose is 1 puff.
steps.picture_prompt: A pharmacist behind a counter holding an inhaler box and a folded leaflet, talking to a customer

steps.text_en: Adults may take up to 2 puffs if needed.
steps.picture_prompt: A pharmacist behind a counter holding an inhaler box and a folded leaflet, talking to a customer

steps.text_en: Ask your pharmacist how many puffs to take.
steps.picture_prompt: A pharmacist behind a counter holding an inhaler box and a folded leaflet, talking to a customer

steps.text_en: Do not use your inhaler more than 4 times in 24 hours.
steps.picture_prompt: A simple round clock with no numbers beside an inhaler, and a doctor listening to a patient

steps.text_en: Do not take more than 8 puffs in 24 hours.
steps.picture_prompt: A simple round clock with no numbers beside an inhaler, and a doctor listening to a patient

steps.text_en: Do not use it more often than advised.
steps.picture_prompt: A simple round clock with no numbers beside an inhaler, and a doctor listening to a patient

steps.text_en: Tell your doctor if your usual dose stops working.
steps.picture_prompt: A simple round clock with no numbers beside an inhaler, and a doctor listening to a patient

steps.text_en: Call 999 if you have severe difficulty breathing. Call 999 if your face or lips swell.
steps.picture_prompt: A person holding a mobile phone to their ear, looking worried, with a ambulance parked outside the window
